title: The Side of Me You Don’t See
description: *I wrote what follows at 5:11 a.m., sitting on my bathroom floor. I decided not to publish it immediately. I’ve had over a good deal of time to sit with it since, and I’ve decided I want you to read it exactly as I wrote it that morning, as it shows a part of me you don’t normally see. I’ve written millions of words that have been distributed to the public. But the thousand that follow may be the hardest I’ve ever had to write. And I’m going to tell you exactly how I’m writing them: undignified, in the bathroom, alternating between being curled over on the toilet, my laptop perched on a stool, and lying on the floor, specifically on my right side, because lying on my left is too painful. I’m writing this in fits and starts, embarrassed, a bit ashamed, and writing it out of an obligation to a promise that I made to myself that maybe I haven’t been good enough at holding up. It’s a promise I also made to you: to be authentic. Sorry for the dramatic opener. It is sincere, but now let me rewind a little bit. Many of you who follow me know my backstory. Around when I was graduating college and starting graduate school, I was very sick with inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis. I shit blood twelve to twenty times per day. I spent a lot of time in excruciating physical pain, which was not even the half of it. I know I’m not the only human to have some form of psychological torture, and a lot of us don’t talk about it. But it stripped everything from me: my physical health, my social life, my romantic prospects, and threatened my career trajectory. The story I tell, which is sincere, is that I found something that effectively put my disease into remission, and allowed me to regain life. None of that’s changed.

title: This Gut Health Breakthrough Is a GLP-1 Gamechanger
description: Scientists have just developed a first-of-its-kind living drug: a probiotic engineered to make GLP-1 inside your gut. And it could change how we think about GLP-1 drugs, and much more. Now, to be clear, when I say “living drug,” I mean that literally. Imagine swallowing a pill containing microscopic living cells engineered to sit in your gut, sense the sugar in what you eat, and release GLP-1 precisely when your body needs it. It’s basically a tiny pharmacy working inside you. And that raises some big questions. Could something like this eventually make GLP-1 injections obsolete? And how could this technology evolve from here? We’ll get into all of that. But first, what were the headline results? *Premium members have been telling me how much they enjoy these little video inserts. And as long as you keep enjoying them, I’ll keep making them! So much fun to level up together. In a new paper just published in Nature , researchers tested the living drug in mice and monkeys. The living drug: Lowered blood sugar Improved insulin sensitivity Increased fat burning Improved body composition And reduced inflammation So, let’s unpack what they built, what the data show, and why I think this strange little living pill offers a glimpse into the future of medicine. How Do You Build a Living Drug? Let me walk you through what the researchers actually engineered. The team started with a well-known probiotic bacterium called E. coli Nissle 1917 , a strain that’s been used safely in humans for over a century.

title: How to Hack Your Brown Fat for Better Health
description: There’s a special type of fat in your body that burns calories like a literal furnace. A major new study , published just a few days ago, now links it to better cardiovascular health, metabolic health, and even mental health. It’s called brown fat. And there are at least 4 different ways to turn it on. In fact, I’ve used one of these myself to burn over 600 more Calories per day without any change in activity, drawing on insights from another randomized controlled trial I’m going to tell you about later. But first, let’s review these new data and what they really mean. Oh, wait! One more teaser before we begin. In case you’ve already seen the headlines around this paper, I promise I have some extra nuances for you, including a paradox buried in the paper itself that hasn’t been discussed. Once I show it to you, I think you’ll understand why I find it particularly interesting. But I’m getting ahead of myself. Let’s understand what makes brown fat special, and the describe the headline findings. What Makes Brown Fat Special? Most of the fat on your body is white fat. White fat is like your lazy friend who walks 2,000 steps a day and hates exercise, whereas you, my brown bestie (okay, that didn’t come out right), are a ball of endless energy! But in all seriousness, brown fat is built differently. Brown fat cells are crammed with mitochondria, which give the tissue its brownish tint because mitochondria are packed with iron. And those mitochondria are the literal engines of your cells. However, they don’t just generate energy for your muscles to use; they also generate heat energy through a different pathway that runs through something called uncoupling proteins (UCP), in particular UCP1.
